messages.author: 235dd2c6f7281965
messages.subject: CALCULATING PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE
parts:
Hello everyone and congratulations on this very useful forum.

I am doing my first analysis with distance sampling for my thesis. My work is based on linear transects and for each observation I record my GPS co-ordinate, the distance to the object (r) and the angle with respect to North (a).
How can I quickly calculate the perpendicular distance of the object (of unknown co-ordinates) to the transect?
Obviously the transect is not perfectly linear but follows the course of the terrain and is not oriented in a north-south direction so I can't simply apply the trigonometric formula x=r*sin(a).

Is there any application on GIS or something similar?

Thank you very much for your reply and good work to everyone!!

Riccardo

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] CALCULATING PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE
parts:
Riccardo

Welcome to the forum. The problem you face is your interpretation of the bearing angle you needed to record in the field. Distance sampling used the perpendicular distance from the transect to account for undetected animals, by computing a detection probability.

The perpendicular distances from the transect at the time of detection can be derived by recording distance to the object (as you have done) and the bearing angle from the direction of the transect (which you have not done).  The angle you need to record in the field is that shown as the red arc below
This is independent of the orientation of the transect itself.

Yes, I know the useful angle to record is that of the object to the transect line, but how do I record the angle from the transect in the field? 
In addition, the transects are not linear so during the journey how could I know the angle between the object and the specific point of the transect where I am? The only data that I can collect in the field is the angle with respect to the North with the compass ....

What I was wondering is if there are quick methods to deduce the position and therefore the perpendicular distance of the object from the closest point to the transect from the data I have available.

Thanks again

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] CALCULATING PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE
parts:
Riccardo

Accurate estimation distances from object to transect requires knowledge not only of where the animal is located, but also where the line is located.

The manual way of determining bearing to animal from the line in the field is to stand where the detection was made, face the direction of the transect (implying you know the bearing of the transect), determine the deflection from the direction of the transect to the direction of the animal. Shipboard survey folk use angle boards to determine deflection (degrees off the bow)



You could conjure something similar for terrestrial surveys.

Very similar suggestions can be found in Section 7.4.2 (Angle measurement) in Buckland et al. (2001).

Given you do not know the coordinates of the object, you cannot compute the shortest distance between the (unknown coordinate) object and the transect line.
